bullets.title: META: Massive AI compute expansion + monetization clarity drives 5-10% rally; $790 PT at KeyBanc
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis report confirmed META's 14GW compute plan for 2027 (~$250B capex) and Muse Spark 1.1 frontier model at 25% cheaper pricing than OpenAI/Anthropic. KeyBanc raised PT to $790 (2028E P/E 20x bull case $1,065); MS TMT flags Zuckerberg confirmed all compute is needed while exploring external cloud sales. Stock ripped 4-8% intraday with unusual call option activity flagged. EU DSA addictive-design preliminary finding (potential 6% revenue fine) and $1.4T state-penalty claims remain headline risks.

bullets.title: NVDA: MS NDR highlights accelerating growth across labs, hyperscalers, sovereigns; memory shortage to persist 'several years'
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley NDR with Jensen Huang emphasizes NVDA at 50-day MA is attractive; growth broadening across AI labs (20% of demand), hyperscalers (50%), and AI clouds/industrial/enterprise (50% of data centers, highest growth). NVDA reconfirmed Vera Rubin Ultra roadmap on track. ~$5M unusual short-dated put block noted. Citi maintains $300 PT/Buy. Kyber NVL144 PCB delay to 2028 is a near-term negative flagged by SemiAnalysis (denied by NVDA).

bullets.title: MU: $250B US investment commitment through 2035; NY fab foundation poured; 2026 earnings to exceed 35 prior years combined
bullets.body: Micron raised US capex to >$250B through 2035 (from $200B), started concrete work on Clay, NY Terafab, and signed long-term SCA with Ford. Analyst Adam Parker calls MU highest-conviction AI semi at 4-5x peak earnings with structural DRAM shortage extending to 2Q28. HBM TAM modeled at $65B in 2026 (+94% YoY) and $129B in 2027 per JPM. JPM bullish entering 2H on CoWoS constraints; top picks include MU alongside AVGO, MRVL, NVDA.

bullets.title: NFLX: Engagement decline deepens; exploring live TV, Peacock bundles; JPM keeps OW at $118 PT
bullets.body: JPM 2Q preview (report July 16): global DAU down 6% YoY despite 8% subscriber growth; US viewership fell to 7.8% TV share in April (low since May 2025); internal quality metric at ATH but bears focused on multiple compression to traditional media 8-13x PE. Stock down 40%+ past 12 months per GS. Citi cuts PT to $100 (25x 2027E EPS from 28x), maintains Buy. Live TV channel and Peacock bundling discussions ongoing. World Cup hurt H1 net adds. Bernstein outperform $100 PT; Citizens sees NBCU acquisition logic.

bullets.title: AVGO: $30B+ multiyear Apple deal through 2031 for custom AI ASIC and RF; FY28 XPV financing a key catalyst
bullets.body: Broadcom expanded AAPL partnership to >$30B through 2031, producing 15B+ US chips and expanding Fort Collins facility by $1.5B. Deal includes AI/datacenter server ASIC (meaningful ramp 2029/30). Wolfe Research maintains $500 OW after mgmt meeting: FY27 demand significantly exceeds guidance, 1GW Anthropic capacity FY26 growing to 6GW+ in FY27; FY28 XPV financing completion ($20GW) is primary catalyst. Erste downgraded to hold; stock +3-4%.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Cloud and Search momentum; KeyBanc raises PT to $445; Marvell DSP role in coherent optics buildout
bullets.body: KeyBanc raises PT to $445 (25x 2028E P/E); 2Q Cloud revenue forecast $23.4B (+72% YoY), total backlog to surpass $480B. Google Search CTRs +2.65% YoY in 2Q per Citi channel checks. MS TMT flags Brian Nowak raising 2028 estimates to $300B+ revenue at low-20s EPS multiple; GOOGL designated critical UK financial supplier effective July 13. Coherent-lite technology for 2,000km inter-campus links emerging as meaningful MRVL DSP demand driver.

bullets.title: MSFT: GPT-5.6 default in Copilot; cutting 4,800 Xbox jobs; UK critical supplier designation
bullets.body: GPT-5.6 Sol now preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot per announcement. MSFT also announced 4,800 Xbox job cuts (20% of Xbox workforce), four studios going independent. JPM credit downgraded MSFT on heavy 2026 capex (~$190B) and $9B FY27 refinancing risks. UK designated MSFT as critical third party to financial sector effective July 13 alongside GOOGL/AMZN/ORCL. Starbucks AI tools development could reduce MSFT and IBM software reliance.

bullets.title: AAPL: JPM raises PT to $345 on price elasticity resilience; EU loses DMA gatekeeper challenge; foldable prep
bullets.body: JPM raises PT to $345 (32x CY28E EPS) after modeling shows iPhone/Mac volumes resilient despite ~20% price increases; Pro iPhone mix at 66% with low elasticity. EU court upheld AAPL 'gatekeeper' status for App Store and iOS. AAPL testing CXMT DRAM for China devices. Hedgeye initiates short at $313.39 with 23% downside. Foldable iPhone priced $2,299–$2,499 entering production, 10M units planned for 2026.

bullets.title: CIEN: Raymond James street-high thesis; TAM doubles to $50B; Amazon DSP win displaces Cisco/Acacia
bullets.body: Citi reports CIEN secured DSP+ win with Amazon for WAN, displacing Cisco/Acacia. Raymond James maintains Street-high estimates post-CFO meetings: FY28 bull case EPS $20 vs. Street $14.28; ~30% pullback creates buying opportunity; scale-across market projected to reach $8-10B by 2029. New products (Vespa) sampling with hyperscalers. META and Google are top two customers driving scale-across adoption.

bullets.title: WULF: Anthropic 20-year, $19B Justified Data lease signals AI power demand; Citi raises PT to $36
bullets.body: TeraWulf announced 401MW lease with Anthropic at Justified Data Campus, KY generating ~$19B contracted revenue over initial term; 22% implied yield exceeds HUT precedent (18.6%). WULF also sold Abernathy JV stake to Fluidstack at premium to recycle capital. MS raises PT to $72 from $66.50 on 'time-to-power' premium. Citi maintains Buy at $36 PT. IREN +13% on Anthropic Australia data center news; Horizon 1 handover confirmed July 19.

bullets.title: SHOP: Stifel upgrades to Buy, raises PT to $150 from $110; Q2 expects 30-31% revenue growth
bullets.body: Stifel upgraded SHOP to buy from hold with $150 PT (+22% upside). BofA also reinstated Buy with $150 PT. KeyBanc raised WSM PT to $250. Analyst tracking Q2 guide of 30-31% revenue growth, 28-30% GMV growth; consensus needs mid-to-high 20% Q3 guidance to support stock. UBS hosting Shopify Payments expert call July 17 on PSP competitive dynamics.

bullets.title: DIS: Exploring free tier for Disney+; YouTube drawing TV viewers accelerating ad-supported pivot
bullets.body: Disney discussing enabling free-tier content on Disney+ per multiple sources. Citi TMT notes free streamers now 18.7% of US TV watch time (up from 12.7% two years prior). JPM Tech Sketch flagged Netflix, Disney, YouTube considering competing for 2030/2034 World Cup rights. Disney+/Hulu bundle at $11.99-17.99/month remains primary paid tier.

bullets.title: FOXA: Rothschild upgrades to Buy with $71 PT (+32%) on Roku deal valuation upside
bullets.body: Rothschild & Co Redburn upgraded FOXA to buy from neutral, raising PT to $71 from $48 citing valuation and upside from Roku deal. FOXA facing headwinds from Netflix/Disney/YouTube challenging Fox for US World Cup broadcast rights through 2030/2034.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: States set to sue to block Paramount-Skydance Warner deal; Arete downgrades PSKY to Sell at $2
bullets.body: California-led states expected to file lawsuit to block PSKY's acquisition of WBD citing antitrust and $80B debt burden concerns; Oregon AG review pushed deal close to at least July 22. Arete Research downgraded PSKY to sell with $2 PT (79% downside from $9.75). PSKY down 2-4% on news flow.

bullets.title: Rosenblatt: Optical/photonics sector weakness overdone; AAOI/LITE/COHR short sellers lack conviction
bullets.body: Rosenblatt says optical sector shorts have 'zero conviction' and plan to cover before earnings; companies expected to 'smash earnings.' CPO delay reports and China capacity fears cited as drivers of 1-2 month weakness. LITE flagged InP capacity expansion as physical AI infrastructure bottleneck. AXTI, COHR, LITE, AAOI testing 3-month lows with bulls defending support; analyst still too early to call bottom but photonics bear case relies on cyclical oversupply end-game.

bullets.title: STX: Wells Fargo upgrades to Overweight; PT raised to $1,100 from $900 on AI storage demand
bullets.body: Wells Fargo upgraded Seagate Technology to overweight, raising PT to $1,100 from $900 (24% upside) per Aaron Rakers. WDC PT also raised to $730 from $575. STX scheduled to report July 16 with consensus EPS $5.09, revenue $3.49B. Storage names broadly rallied on AI infrastructure demand confirmation.

bullets.title: DKNG: Indiana June sports betting GGR -38% YoY; hold rate compressed 570bps to 7.1%
bullets.body: Indiana June sports betting GGR -18% YoY statewide with handle +15%; overall hold rate declined 370bps to 9.2%. DKNG specifically down -38% YoY with handle +12% YoY and hold rate falling 570bps to 7.1%, market share at 36%. FanDuel GGR -24% YoY. Missouri June casino GGR +2% YoY with PENN properties +4.2%, CZR -5.8%.

bullets.title: TSLA: SPCX-TSLA combination strategically coherent per JPM; robotaxi expands to Miami without safety driver
bullets.body: JPM analysis calls SpaceX-TSLA combination strategically logical given shared engineering talent, AI infrastructure, Terafab facility in Texas—but flags regulatory hurdles (SPCX defense contracts + TSLA China), governance asymmetry (SPCX ~$2.2T > TSLA $1.4T), and SPCX likely acquirer. Tesla launched unsupervised robotaxi service in Miami (first non-Texas market), operating ~59 robotaxis. TSLA down 10% YTD vs Nasdaq +16%.

bullets.title: GEV/ENPH: Power infrastructure names as AI beat-and-raise candidates; 800VDC data center transition next catalyst
bullets.body: OPCO sees GEV and ENPH as top picks for beat-and-raise results as data centers migrate to 800V architectures. Morgan Stanley raised FSLR PT to $245, affirmed bullish BE outlook at $310. PJM power margin rally on hot weather/load growth driving TLN, CEG, VST upside risk; 2028/2029 capacity auction results expected Tuesday. Deutsche Bank upgraded FSLR to buy from hold, raising PT to $272 from $245.

bullets.title: Goldman: AI-driven memory/software/electricity prices adding 0.5% to core PCE by year-end; Fed MPR flags chip costs
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs estimates AI-induced increases in memory, software, and electricity prices contributing >0.2% to YoY core PCE currently, rising to 0.5% by year-end. Fed's semi-annual monetary policy report explicitly cited memory and chip prices as driving core inflation higher alongside tariffs and Middle East factors. SK Hynix CEO warns memory shortage could persist past 2030. Jefferies raises China AI capex forecasts 23% to $1T through 2030.
